title: Verifier‑Grounded Paired Test of Intent→Config Generation (estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; shared_initial_candidate semantics)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that measured a verifier‑grounded estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) under preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics. Using gpt‑5‑mini (declared_model_version) and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), we ran N=120 synthetic intent→config tasks with exhaustive artifacts archived. Result: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared_initial seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap seed 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (i) publish the exact execution and per‑episode validator traces needed for byte‑for‑byte reproduction (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the artifact bundle), (ii) diagnose—using archived artifacts—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a degenerate paired contingency (identical canonical candidates + template‑tight tasks + deterministic validator), and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory designs, validator diversification, and task heterogeneity expansion) that preserve reproducibility while yielding an informative estimate of independent generative reliability. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Automated translation from operator intent to device configuration is central to NetOps; correctness is safety‑critical because misordered or missing commands can break reachability or violate transient constraints during multi‑step changes. We preregistered a narrow, verifier‑grounded estimand—paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline—with the explicit generation_semantics shared_initial_candidate so that each task pair would be scored on the identical canonical candidate. The choice isolates the deterministic validator’s behavior under identical inputs rather than measuring independent stochastic generation reliability. Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, reproducible execution and analysis bundle (preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...); (2) confirmatory counts and preregistered inference grounded in archived traces (baseline = 120/120; guarded = 120/120; paired diff = 0.00; 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0); and (3) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis and runnable corrections that convert the current design into one that estimates independent generative reliability without losing determinism or reproducibility.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation is an established operational pattern: offline analyzers such as Batfish and successors compute forwarding/reachability and detect ACL/routing policy violations from static configs and are used in pre‑deployment validation [Brown et al., 2023; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps work typically couples generation to deterministic verifiers in generate–validate–repair loops; designs differ in sampling semantics (single candidate vs. independent multi‑seed), repair budgets (single pass vs. bounded iterative loops), and validator scope (syntax vs. reachability+ACL+transient checks). The literature shows most repair gains accrue in early repair iterations and that orchestration/feedback design often dominates raw model choice for end‑to‑end reliability (see recent repair/iterative loop surveys). Our study sits within this verifier‑grounded lineage but intentionally tests a different estimand (validator consistency under identical inputs) and therefore complements independent‑sampling evaluations.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663c...) fixed: N = 120 paired intent→config tasks (40 per topology class), model = gpt‑5‑mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0), primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 with bootstrap resamples = 10,000 (seed = 1729). All code, seeds, provider traces, canonical responses, and validator JSON traces were archived in the execution bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json) with per‑file SHA‑256s.
Task synthesis and templates. Tasks were programmatically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and embed explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies (must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups, final_group_constraints). These templates encode operational transient constraints (make‑before‑break, atomic MTU changes, rolling VLAN migration) so that passing the validator requires both correct sequencing and preserved invariants. Representative task manifests and canonical shared candidates are archived (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., task‑000002 SHA‑256 ae967f70..., task‑000003 SHA‑256 f7f4db24...).
Model calls, shared_initial semantics, and scoring. For each task the pipeline generated one canonical candidate (shared_initial) using gpt‑5‑mini and then scored that identical candidate under two labeled episodes (baseline and guarded) using deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Scoring produced a detailed validator trace per episode (execution/scoring/*.json). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 120, planned_episode_count = 240, completed_episode_count = 240, and failed_episode_count = 0; full accounting is available in execution/execution_manifest.json (artifact SHA list). Contamination heuristics (exact match and normalized n‑gram overlap) were run as preregistered and recorded in analysis/contamination_summary.csv.
sections.results:
Confirmatory counts and preregistered inference (artifact‑grounded). All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed and are archived. The raw paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...) is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0; baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. The paired estimator (mean guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. The preregistered bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) produced 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.00]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 (analysis artifacts and log archived: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 ff20bc07...). Representative per‑episode validator traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...) record parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, and validation_after.valid = true; these files demonstrate that the canonical candidates satisfy the task‑encoded required_sequences and transient constraints.
Causal diagnosis grounded in artifacts. The degenerate paired contingency is a direct, artifact‑visible consequence of two preregistered design choices archived in the bundle: (1) the shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one canonical LLM candidate per task reused verbatim across both scoring episodes; see execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt, representative SHA‑256s above), and (2) template‑tight tasks that include explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies satisfied by canonical, template‑aligned candidates. Because the validator is deterministic, identical inputs necessarily yield identical pass/fail outputs. The deterministic accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s in execution/execution_manifest.json permit byte‑for‑byte reproduction of this causal chain.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and what the confirmatory test does (and does not) show. The confirmatory test correctly answers its preregistered estimand: whether a deterministic validator treats identical artifacts differently under two scoring labels; it does not estimate independent generative reliability (the probability that independently sampled LLM outputs will satisfy verifier constraints in deployment). That operational quantity requires independent_per_condition sampling (different seeds per condition) or multi‑seed replication per condition; the archived pipeline supports deterministic reruns to answer that question without changing task templates. Runnable artifact‑grounded modifications. The archived bundle supports immediate, deterministic reruns that produce informative operational estimates: (A) independent_per_condition rerun — generate distinct seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1) and rescore using the same validator; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory execution — draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification — introduce a second independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates to reduce validator–task coupling. Because all generator code, model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), provider call traces, and validator code are archived and fingerprinted, these reruns are deterministic and reproducible.
Threats to validity (artifact‑verified). Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate removed generation variance by design, so the confirmatory contrast tests validator determinism rather than generative reliability. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks plus a single deterministic validator can overestimate apparent success when canonical candidates reproduce template patterns. External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic tasks, and single validator limit generalization. Conclusion validity: degenerate 2×2 table yields trivially exact inference for the preregistered estimand but is uninformative about independent stochastic behavior. All these threats are documented and supported by the archived traces.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released a complete artifact bundle enabling byte‑level reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120). Archived evidence—canonical candidate files and per‑episode validator traces—shows that identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight task constraints caused the degenerate paired outcome; consequently the confirmatory paired result does not provide evidence about independent LLM generative reliability. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmation, validator diversity) that preserve reproducibility and enable informative independent comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts, including the immutable initial master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e...), are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, removing independent sampling variance and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
